candidates.issues: None. Excellent method—rubbing oil into the panko ensures an even, crispy, golden crust in the oven without deep frying.
Drizzling oil directly over wet batter on a baking sheet is an uneven method that can cause the batter to slide off or clump rather than crisping nicely.
Drizzling oil over panko after coating can result in uneven crisping; spraying the oil or pre-mixing it into the crumbs works better. Otherwise, a very solid recipe.
Baking the glazed cauliflower for 8 minutes at 450°F (230°C) is very risky; the honey and gochujang will likely burn at that temperature.
The batter ratio (1.5 cups dry ingredients to 0.75 cups water) is completely off; it will create a thick paste or dough rather than a dippable batter.
The batter ratio is slightly on the thin side, which might struggle to adhere well to smooth cauliflower without a pre-dredge, but deep frying is the most authentic method for a takeout-style crunch.
